summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of ankylosing spondylitis, severe obesity, hypertension, asthma, and obstructive sleep apnea, was admitted for acute on chronic left lower back and sacroiliac pain rated 10/10. He reported symptoms typical of prior flares and requested prednisone and opioids for relief. Evaluation revealed mild elevation in inflammatory markers (CRP 12.4, ESR 38) but no signs of infection or acute pathology. Rheumatology and chronic pain consultations did not support steroid use, instead recommending NSAIDs, muscle relaxants, and physical therapy, all of which the patient declined due to prior side effects or concerns. His home pain regimen, including oxycodone and oxycontin, was continued, and tizanidine was increased to 4 mg BID PRN. The patient expressed dissatisfaction but agreed to follow up with rheumatology to discuss restarting biologic therapy pending infectious workup results. He was discharged home in stable condition after two days with plans for outpatient follow-up.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
